advisories.detail: lem:classical-kneser-spectrum: depends on lem:johnson-kneser-adjacency-eigenvalue (statement-uses) but never references \cref{obj:lem:johnson-kneser-adjacency-eigenvalue}

synth_1.title: Feasible schedule array
synth_1.body:
A feasible triangular schedule array with common group size \(M\) consists of the following data:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Group size.)} A natural number \(M\) satisfying \(2\le M\).
\item \textbf{(Row sizes.)} For each row \(r\in\mathbb N\), a population size \(n_r\in\mathbb N\), a number of groups \(G_r\in\mathbb N\), and a number of treated groups \(G_{1r}\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Feasibility.)} For every row \(r\),
\[
0<G_r,\qquad M G_r\le n_r,\qquad 0<G_{1r},\qquad G_{1r}<G_r,\qquad G_{1r}\le G_r .
\]
\item \textbf{(Potential-outcome schedule.)} For every row \(r\), a deterministic potential-outcome schedule
\[
Y_r:\Omega_{n_r,M}\to \{i\in \{0,\ldots,n_r-1\}: i\in A\}\to \mathcal Z\to \mathbb R,
\]
where \(A\in\Omega_{n_r,M}\) is the realized group argument of \(Y_r\).
\end{itemize}

synth_2.title: Treatment-arm set
synth_2.body:
The treatment-arm set is the two-point set
\[
\mathcal Z=\{0,1\}.
\]

synth_3.title: Uniform slice averaging
synth_3.body:
For integers \(M\le n\), let
\[
\Omega_{n,M}:=\{A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}: |A|=M\}.
\]
The \(M\)-slice design is the complete-randomization design on \(\Omega_{n,M}\), equivalently the uniform distribution over all \(M\)-element subsets of the \(n\)-unit population. For any real-valued table \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\), write
\[
\mathbb E_n f
:=
\frac{1}{|\Omega_{n,M}|}\sum_{A\in\Omega_{n,M}} f(A).
\]

synth_4.title: Uniform-slice norm
synth_4.body:
For integers \(M \le n\), let
\[
\Omega_{n,M}:=\{A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}: |A|=M\}.
\]
For any real-valued function \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\), define its squared uniform-slice norm by
\[
\|f\|_n^2
:=
\langle f,f\rangle_n
:=
\mathbb E_n\{f(A)^2\},
\]
where \(\mathbb E_n\) denotes averaging over the uniform law on \(\Omega_{n,M}\).

synth_5.title: Centered arm table
synth_5.body:
For integers \(n\) and \(M\) with \(M\le n\), let
\[
\Omega_{n,M}=\{A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}: |A|=M\}.
\]
Given a deterministic potential-outcome schedule \(Y_{i,n}(z,A)\) for units \(i\in A\), arms \(z\in\mathcal Z\), and groups \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), define the centered arm-\(z\) group table by
\[
h_{z,n}^{\circ}(A)
=
h_{z,n}(A)-\mathbb E_n[h_{z,n}]
\]
for each \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), where
\[
h_{z,n}(A)=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{i\in A}Y_{i,n}(z,A),
\qquad
\mathbb E_n[h_{z,n}]
=
\frac{1}{|\Omega_{n,M}|}\sum_{B\in\Omega_{n,M}} h_{z,n}(B).
\]

synth_6.title: Same-sign schedule prior
synth_6.body:
For each \(n\), \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) is the finite product design on Boolean schedules \(h:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{0,1\}\) whose coordinate design at every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is the fair coin design:
\[
\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}
:=
\bigotimes_{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}}
\operatorname{Coin}\!\left(\frac12\right).
\]

synth_7.title: Independent sign prior
synth_7.body:
For a population size \(n\), \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\) is the product finite design on arrays \(h:\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}\) under which every unit-arm coordinate is drawn independently from the fair two-point law:
\[
\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}
=
\bigotimes_{(i,z)\in \{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\}}
\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\frac12\right).
\]

synth_8.title: One-realization observation
synth_8.body:
A one-realization observation \(\mathcal O_n\) at population size \(n\), common group size \(M\), realized group count \(G_n\), and treated-group count \(G_{1n}\) is a triple
\[
\mathcal O_n=(\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n,Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_n)
\]
with the following components:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Partition.)} \(\mathbf A_n=(A_{g,n})_{g=1}^{G_n}\) is an ordered tuple with \(A_{g,n}\in\Omega_{n,M}\) for every \(g\), and \(A_{g,n}\cap A_{g',n}=\varnothing\) whenever \(g\ne g'\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment allocation.)} \(\mathbf Z_n\) selects a subset of the realized groups with exactly \(G_{1n}\) elements.
\item \textbf{(Observed outcomes.)} For every realized group \(g\) and every unit \(i\in A_{g,n}\), \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_n\) assigns a real observed outcome \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,g,n}\in\mathbb R\).
\end{itemize}

synth_9.title: Realized arm group counts
synth_9.body:
For \(z\in\mathcal Z=\{0,1\}\), let
\[
G_{z,n}=\sum_{g=1}^{G_n}\mathbf 1\{Z_{ng}=z\}
\]
be the number of realized groups assigned to arm \(z\) at row \(n\). Under the complete group-treatment assignment with exactly \(G_{1n}\) treated groups and \(G_{0n}=G_n-G_{1n}\) control groups, this notation gives \(G_{1,n}=G_{1n}\) and \(G_{0,n}=G_{0n}\).

synth_10.title: Johnson and Kneser covariance apparatus
synth_10.body:
For \(0\le k\le M\), let \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\subseteq L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) be the degree-\(k\) Johnson harmonic subspace, and let \(\Pi_{n,k}\) be the \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\)-orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\). For \(f\in L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\), the centered Johnson decomposition is
\[
f-\mathbb E_n f=\sum_{k=1}^M\Pi_{n,k}f.
\]
For \(2M\le n\), the unnormalized Kneser adjacency operator is
\[
(\mathrm{Adj}_{n,M}f)(A)=\sum_{\substack{C\in\Omega_{n,M}\\ C\cap A=\varnothing}} f(C),
\qquad A\in\Omega_{n,M}.
\]
The normalized Kneser disjointness operator is
\[
(\mathsf K_n f)(A)=\binom{n-M}{M}^{-1}
\sum_{\substack{C\in\Omega_{n,M}\\ C\cap A=\varnothing}} f(C).
\]
Its eigenvalue on \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) is denoted by \(\lambda_{n,k}\). For \(a,b\in\mathcal Z\), define the ordered-disjoint covariance and the arm-difference covariance by
\[
C_{ab,n}=\langle h_{a,n}^{\circ},\mathsf K_n h_{b,n}^{\circ}\rangle_n,\qquad
C_{\tau\tau,n}=C_{11,n}+C_{00,n}-2C_{10,n}.
\]
The degree-one arm-difference energy is
\[
E_{\tau,1,n}=\|\Pi_{n,1}(h_{1,n}-h_{0,n})\|_n^2.
\]

synth_11.title: Row treatment fraction
synth_11.body:
For a triangular schedule array with row group count \(G_n\) and treated-group count \(G_{1n}\), where \(0<G_{1n}<G_n\), the row treatment fraction is
\[
p_n=\frac{G_{1n}}{G_n}.
\]

synth_12.title: Uniform-slice \(L^2\) space
synth_12.body:
For integers \(n\) and \(M\) with \(2M\le n\), let \(\mathcal U_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and
\[
\Omega_{n,M}=\{A\subseteq\mathcal U_n: |A|=M\}
\]
be the uniform \(M\)-slice. The space \(L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) is the real vector space of functions \(f:\Omega_{n,M}\to\mathbb R\), equipped with uniform-slice expectation
\[
\mathbb E_n f=\binom nM^{-1}\sum_{A\in\Omega_{n,M}} f(A),
\]
inner product
\[
\langle f,g\rangle_n=\mathbb E_n[fg],
\]
and induced norm \(\|f\|_n^2=\langle f,f\rangle_n\).
